hypoxia induces apoptosis or mitosis, depending on the severity of the hypoxic stress, by triggering timed expression of cell cycle and apoptosis proteins.
hypoxia induces apoptosis and neurogenesis in developing brain neurons by triggering the expression of cell cycle- and apoptosis-related proteins, respectively.

a new hypothesis that cell cycle re-entry may precede neuronal death, and that cell fate may depend on the balance between pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic signals.
the mechanisms underlying cell fate in neuronal response to transient hypoxia, in relation with the cell cycle.
the molecular mechanisms of neuronal cell cycle activation and its relation to neuronal death and survival.

hypoxia, whatever the stress level, induces cell cycle activation, but that the fate of the cell is determined by a balance between survival and death signals.
the cell cycle machinery is activated in response to hypoxic insult, whatever the intensity of the stress.
hypoxia-induced cell death and survival in the developing brain share the same molecular pathway.

the cell cycle is a major target of hypoxia and that cell fate is dependent on the intensity of hypoxic insult.
severe hypoxia induces apoptosis, while mild hypoxia promotes survival, by triggering cell cycle and neurogenic processes.

hypoxia can induce either cell cycle activation or apoptosis, depending on the severity of the insult, and that both processes are regulated by common molecular mechanisms.
